If you’re buying satin bonnets because you think they’re basically the same thing as silk, PLEASE learn from my mistake. 😭 I spent years buying cheap satin bonnets thinking I was protecting my hair while I slept. They felt smooth, they said “satin” on the package... what more did I need to know?

Apparently, A LOT. 😂

Satin and silk are not the same thing. Satin refers to the weave, and many inexpensive satin bonnets are actually made from synthetic materials like polyester. Blissy’s bonnets are made with real silk and double-lined so my hair is surrounded by that incredibly smooth surface all night.

Once I switched to Blissy, I finally understood why people spend the extra money on real silk. My hair looks smoother when I wake up, I deal with way less frizz and tangling, and my styles actually have a chance of surviving the night. The smooth silk helps reduce the friction, pulling, and tugging my hair goes through while I toss and turn, while also helping it retain its natural moisture overnight. 🙌

And unlike half the bonnets I’ve tried that somehow ended up on the other side of my bed by morning, my Blissy actually stays on my head. 😂

I genuinely thought I was saving money by buying cheap satin bonnets. Then I realized I was spending way more money trying to fix the frizz, breakage, and bedhead afterward.

If you’re serious about protecting your hair, skip the satin and go for the real thing.
